items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: Well, Frank Drake's got all of this information from me.

ctx.x: Well, it's a shame to let all this material not get published, and yet it's hard to find anybody who's interested in it. Right, they're interested in it. And they publish, you know, really second-rate books and all of that. And certainly if anybody knows about Kansas City music and Texas and Oklahoma and all that is Frank Drake. And I think everybody in the business knows that.
Well, Frank Drake's got all of this information from me. Yeah.
But I mean, he's the one who's done the most writing. Right. And then, uh...

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: In fact I had my friend in New York City has often tried to get someone interested in this, Franklin Dregs.

ctx.x: That would be wonderful. We'd like to hear you again. I know a lot of people would.

You certainly would. Well in fact I'm doing it mostly for some friends out of New Orleans that have dug up some of this jazz history on my background and I feel that if it's in my power to come back and do the things that I know how to do in music and if it'll make someone else happy along with making me happy which is the fundamental thing well I'm more than happy to do so. In fact I had my friend in New York City has often tried to get someone interested in this, Franklin Dregs.
I know he's been interested in for years in the music of the whole southwest as he calls it from Kansas City on down to Oklahoma and Texas. That's right. He's been quite a number of articles on that.
